definitions.gloss: copyright; intellectual property rights (for creative works)
definitions.explanation: The legal right of a creator to control the reproduction, distribution, and adaptation of their original work, including written works, music, art, and software.

examples.japanese: この{写真|しゃしん}の{著作権|ちょさくけん}は{撮影者|さつえいしゃ}にある。
examples.english: The copyright for this photo belongs to the photographer.

examples.japanese: {著作権|ちょさくけん}を{侵害|しんがい}すると{法的|ほうてき}{責任|せきにん}を{問|と}われる。
examples.english: Violating copyright can result in legal liability.

examples.japanese: インターネット{上|じょう}のコンテンツにも{著作権|ちょさくけん}があるので、{無断|むだん}で{転載|てんさい}してはいけない。
examples.english: Online content is also protected by copyright, so you must not repost it without permission.

notes:
A compound of {著作|ちょさく} (authorship, literary work) and {権|けん} (right). One of the most important legal terms in modern Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {著作権|ちょさくけん}を{侵害|しんがい}する (infringe copyright)
- {著作権|ちょさくけん}を{保護|ほご}する (protect copyright)
- {著作権|ちょさくけん}{法|ほう} (copyright law)
- {著作権|ちょさくけん}フリー (copyright-free, royalty-free)
- {著作権|ちょさくけん}の{切|き}れた (out of copyright, in the public domain)

Japanese copyright law ({著作権法|ちょさくけんほう}) generally protects works for 70 years after the death of the author. The term has become increasingly important in discussions about AI-generated content and digital media.
